sections.Intro: This remedy is characterized by a general feeling of heaviness and congestion, especially in the portal system and the rectum. It is useful in cases of haemorrhoids and chronic diarrhoea. There is a general lack of control over the anal sphincter. The patient is often a large, phlegmatic person. There is a marked tendency to portal congestion.
sections.Mind: Confused. Forgetful. Aversion to mental and physical labor.
sections.Head: Headache, with a sensation of weight in the forehead. Vertigo.
sections.Eyes: Eyes red and burning. Sensation of heat.
sections.Mouth: Metallic taste. Tongue yellow and coated.
sections.Stomach: Appetite poor. Thirst. Heaviness and pressure after eating.
sections.Abdomen: Distended and tender. Rumbling. Flatulence. Sharp pains in the region of the liver.
sections.Rectum: Haemorrhoids, like bunches of grapes; purple, painful, and itching. Anus feels as if it were open. Constant desire for stool. Stool passes involuntarily while urinating or passing gas. Diarrhoea of thin, watery stools, with much gas.
sections.Urinary: Frequent desire to urinate. Scanty urine.
sections.Extremities: Aching and lameness in the limbs. Heaviness in the legs.
sections.Modalities: Worse in the morning and in hot weather. Better from cold applications and in the open air.
sections.Relationship: Compare: Aesculus; Collinsonia; Nux vom.; Sulphur.
